concepts.title: Meaning and Many Views of Work
concepts.definition: Purposeful human effort, paid or unpaid, through which a person earns a living, uses personal talent, builds relations and finds a place in society.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- work can be seen as job, duty, dharma, calling or self development
concepts.key_idea: Work is more than wages: it shapes identity, dignity and contribution to family, employer and society.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Work and Meaningful Work (approx lines 50-130)
question_patterns: what do you understand by the term work
explain any four ways in which work can be viewed
how does work help a person fit into society
why do people say work keeps the machine of society running
list the factors that decide the type of work a person takes up
state why unpaid family work still counts as work

solution_steps.action: recall that work is purposeful effort, with or without pay
solution_steps.explain: the chapter treats paid jobs, housework and volunteering alike as work

solution_steps.action: list the views: job and living, duty, security, dharma, spiritual practice, joy, status, self development
solution_steps.explain: each view highlights a different reward of working

worked_examples.q: Purposeful human effort through which a person earns a living and finds a place in society is called what?

concepts.title: Meaningful Work
concepts.definition: Effort that helps society or others, is carried out responsibly, is enjoyed by the worker, and leaves room to apply skill, judgment and creativity.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- usefulness plus responsibility plus enjoyment makes effort meaningful
concepts.key_idea: Meaningful effort repays the worker with growth, confidence, self worth and recognition.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, What is meaningful work (approx lines 129-145)
question_patterns: what is meant by meaningful work
state three qualities that make an occupation meaningful
how does meaningful work help personal growth
why may a volunteer without any pay still be doing meaningful work
distinguish between any work and meaningful work with one example
which workplace conditions let a worker show creativity and judgment

solution_steps.action: check the effort against the three markers: useful to others, done responsibly, enjoyed
solution_steps.explain: all three markers together signal meaningfulness

solution_steps.action: add the enabling conditions: use of skill and judgment, creativity, recognition and rewards
solution_steps.explain: these conditions turn an occupation into a source of confidence and worth

worked_examples.q: Effort that helps society, is carried out responsibly and is enjoyed is called what work?

concepts.title: Job versus Career
concepts.definition: A job is engagement in work mainly for earnings, while a career is a sustained climb inside one chosen field, powered by the wish to grow and excel.
concepts.formula: qualitative contrast -- job pays now, career builds over a lifetime
concepts.key_idea: A career needs continual upgrading of skills and knowledge, not just appointment to a post.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, job and career paragraphs plus boulder anecdote (approx lines 168-248)
question_patterns: differentiate between a job and a career
state two features that set a career apart from a job
why is it said that a career is more than just a job
in the stone cutter story, explain how the three men viewed the same task differently
give one example of how a person moves from holding a job to building a career
what does the sculptor in the anecdote teach about vision at work

solution_steps.action: define job: work taken up for the sake of income or duty
solution_steps.explain: the first stone breaker saw only the task at hand

solution_steps.action: define career: a chosen path of progressive achievement
solution_steps.explain: the third man linked every hammer blow to his vision of becoming a sculptor

solution_steps.action: contrast the mindset: satisfaction from pay versus satisfaction from advancement and mastery
solution_steps.explain: career minded workers keep learning and upgrading themselves

worked_examples.q: Engagement in work mainly for earnings is called a what: job or career?

concepts.title: Livelihood and Career Management
concepts.definition: Livelihood is the occupation and means through which a person meets basic needs, while a career is the lifelong, evolving sequence of roles each individual manages.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- career growth means balancing paid work, learning and life roles
concepts.key_idea: Careers are unique and dynamic; managing one means making transitions whenever needed.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Work, Careers and Livelihoods (approx lines 192-214)
question_patterns: what is meant by livelihood
how is a career a life management concept
explain why careers are described as unique and dynamic
which balances must a person maintain while growing a career
how does career development continue through the middle and later years of work life
name the activities other than paid employment that count as work

solution_steps.action: state the livelihood side: occupation chosen to meet needs and sustain lifestyle
solution_steps.explain: livelihood anchors the economic base of a person

solution_steps.action: state the career side: lifelong process of managing roles and transitions
solution_steps.explain: paid and unpaid work, learning and personal roles must stay in balance

worked_examples.q: The occupation and means through which a person meets basic needs is called what?

concepts.title: Traditional Occupations of India
concepts.definition: Farming, fishing, weaving, handicrafts, regional cuisines and visual arts carried across generations form the inherited occupational base of Indian villages, once passed on as guarded home training.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- inherited craft skill sustained rural livelihood for centuries
concepts.key_idea: Mass produced goods, poor finance and weak marketing now squeeze artisan incomes, so revival needs design, training and IPR protection.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Traditional Occupations of India (approx lines 292-428)
question_patterns: name any four traditional occupations of India
why is weaving called a cottage industry in India
what problems do Indian artisans face in the modern market
list the interventions needed to revive and sustain traditional crafts
how do traditional occupations support rural livelihood even today
which crops of economic importance bring India foreign exchange
how was craft knowledge transferred inside families in the past

solution_steps.action: enumerate the occupation groups: farming, fishing, crafts like pottery and embroidery, cuisine, visual arts
solution_steps.explain: each region built its own signature craft and food tradition

solution_steps.action: explain the transmission: skill moved from parents to children inside closed groups
solution_steps.explain: secrecy protected the finer nuances of every craft

solution_steps.action: list the present threats and remedies
solution_steps.explain: design innovation, training facilities, eco friendly materials and IPR cover can restore incomes

worked_examples.q: Which inherited craft has sustained Indian village livelihood for centuries: weaving or software?

concepts.title: Gender, Sex and Women and Work
concepts.definition: Sex sorts people by biology and chromosomes; gender is the social identity and the set of expected roles a culture attaches to being male, female or third gender.
concepts.formula: qualitative contrast -- sex is biological, gender is socially built
concepts.key_idea: Household work done by women is a real economic contribution and must be valued like paid work; working women also carry a double burden of job plus home care.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Gender Issues in Relation to Work and women and work concerns (approx lines 440-576)
question_patterns: distinguish between sex and gender
what does it mean to say that gender is socially constructed
why should the domestic work of women be treated as an economic activity
what is the double burden carried by working women
which constitutional article guarantees equality of opportunity in employment
name the labour laws that protect women workers in India
what is the Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya scheme meant for

solution_steps.action: separate the two terms: biology versus social expectation
solution_steps.explain: chromosomes decide sex; society writes the gender script

solution_steps.action: trace the workplace angle: stereotypes, unpaid home work, double burden
solution_steps.explain: women's earnings are wrongly treated as secondary even when they are sole earners

solution_steps.action: recall the safeguards: equality articles, protective Acts, creche and maternity provisions
solution_steps.explain: equality articles, protective Acts, creche and maternity clauses; state schemes and women's cells push the empowerment agenda

worked_examples.q: Which term sorts people by biology and chromosomes: sex or gender?

concepts.title: Quality of Work Life
concepts.definition: Quality of Work Life is the degree to which a workplace meets the social and psychological needs of employees alongside economic ones, treating people as assets rather than costs.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- fair treatment plus participation plus balance lifts morale and output
concepts.key_idea: Job satisfaction flows more from attitude, fair comparison and growth chances than from pay alone.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Attitudes and Approaches to Work and Quality of Work Life (approx lines 665-769)
question_patterns: explain the term quality of work life
why do organisations treat employees as assets
list any four features of a healthy work environment
how is job satisfaction linked to attitude rather than to salary alone
what steps can a manager take to build a positive work climate
why should comparisons at the workplace include responsibilities and not just pay

solution_steps.action: define the idea: satisfying social and psychological needs along with economic ones
solution_steps.explain: people perform better when conditions feel fair and supportive

solution_steps.action: list the levers: attention to individual needs, positive climate, motivation, fairness, safety, interesting tasks, team spirit, training, empowerment
solution_steps.explain: together these levers create loyalty and better output

worked_examples.q: What does QWL stand for in workplace studies?

concepts.title: Life Skills for Livelihood
concepts.definition: Practical abilities for adaptive, positive conduct that let people handle everyday demands; experts list ten core sets, from self-awareness and empathy through to coping with emotions and stress.
concepts.formula: knowledge plus attitudes plus values lead to life skills and psychosocial competence
concepts.key_idea: Life skills protect health and well being across the lifespan and grow through experience, not lectures.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Life Skills for Livelihood (approx lines 774-829)
question_patterns: what are life skills and why are they important
name the ten core life skills identified by experts
how do life skills promote and protect health and well being
which life skill helps you sense another person's feelings
why can life skills not be picked up from classroom lessons alone
how do knowledge, attitudes and values combine into psychosocial competence

solution_steps.action: define the term: adaptive and positive abilities for daily demands
solution_steps.explain: WHO frames them as thinking, coping and social skills

solution_steps.action: list the ten core sets: self-awareness, empathy, communication, interpersonal relationships, decision making, problem solving, creative thinking, critical thinking, coping with emotions, coping with stress
solution_steps.explain: experiential learning builds these abilities into behaviour

worked_examples.q: How many core life skill sets do experts list: ten or two?

concepts.title: Dignity of Labour, Values and Ethics
concepts.section: Work, Ethics and Dignity of Labour
concepts.definition: Taking pride in every kind of honest effort is the dignity of labour; values are personal beliefs about what is good, while ethics are rule systems that a profession formally adopts.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- respect for every worker plus ethical conduct sustains a workplace
concepts.key_idea: Ethical behaviour cuts waste, lifts morale and raises productivity for everyone around.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Work, Ethics and Dignity of Labour (approx lines 972-1009)
question_patterns: what is meant by dignity of labour
how did Mahatma Gandhi demonstrate the dignity of labour at his ashram
distinguish between values and ethics with one example each
list the six important values named for professional life
how do values and ethics reduce waste and raise productivity at the workplace
why does every worker deserve respect irrespective of position or pay

solution_steps.action: define dignity of labour: pride in whatever task one performs
solution_steps.explain: Gandhi's cleaning of his own quarters is the classic illustration

solution_steps.action: separate values from ethics
solution_steps.explain: values are inner beliefs; ethics are adopted group rules for conduct

worked_examples.q: Taking pride in every kind of honest effort is called the dignity of what: labour or leisure?

concepts.title: Ergonomics at the Workplace
concepts.definition: Built from Greek roots for work and natural laws, ergonomics studies people on the job and reshapes tools, workstations and methods so the workplace fits the worker instead of the reverse.
concepts.formula: goal -- adapt work environment to worker for safety, comfort and productivity
concepts.key_idea: Anthropometry, biomechanics, physiology and industrial psychology are its four pillars; good design cuts injuries, errors and absenteeism.
question_patterns: define ergonomics and trace the origin of the word
what are the four pillars on which the science of ergonomics rests
list the benefits of applying ergonomics in a workplace
why should an office chair be adjustable to the user's body
how does ergonomics improve productivity and job satisfaction together
which factors of the work environment do ergonomists study
why is ergonomics also called human factors engineering

solution_steps.action: define and expand the term: study of humans at work, adapting the environment to the worker
solution_steps.explain: the Greek roots ergon and nomics give the name

solution_steps.action: name the four supporting sciences
solution_steps.explain: body measurement, body mechanics, physiology and industrial psychology

solution_steps.action: state the payoffs: fewer injuries and accidents, higher productivity, fewer mistakes, less absenteeism, better morale
solution_steps.explain: a matched task-worker pair wastes less and errs less

worked_examples.q: Which field reshapes tools and workstations so the workplace fits the worker: ergonomics or economics?

concepts.title: Entrepreneurship and the Entrepreneur
concepts.definition: The act of building a fresh enterprise, product or service by organising resources and finances and by taking calculated risks to turn a novel idea into reality.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- entrepreneur equals innovator plus organiser plus risk taker
concepts.key_idea: Social entrepreneurs chase large scale social benefit and measure success by impact, not profit.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Entrepreneurship and Characteristics of Entrepreneurs (approx lines 1160-1261)
question_patterns: define entrepreneurship in your own words
list any six characteristics of a successful entrepreneur
how does a social entrepreneur differ from a business entrepreneur
why is an entrepreneur called a calculated risk taker
name two celebrated Indian entrepreneurs mentioned in the chapter
what kind of institutions support aspiring entrepreneurs
how can entrepreneurship range from a micro unit to a large undertaking

solution_steps.action: define the venture building act
solution_steps.explain: innovation changes how a product is made or what it offers

solution_steps.action: list personal attributes: hard work, planning, finance and time management, courage, coping with setbacks, networking, negotiation, communication
solution_steps.explain: these attributes let one person carry an idea to market

solution_steps.action: contrast social entrepreneurship with profit seeking ventures
solution_steps.explain: the social variant serves underserved groups and is judged by benefit delivered

worked_examples.q: Building a fresh enterprise by organising resources and taking calculated risks is called what?

concepts.title: Creche Rule of the Factories Act
concepts.section: Constitutional Rights, Acts and The State Initiatives
concepts.definition: Under Section 48 of the Factories Act, an industry that keeps more than thirty women on its rolls must run a creche for children under age six.
concepts.key_idea: A positive excess over the thirty woman mark means the factory has crossed the creche trigger.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe101.txt, Factories Act creche provision (approx lines 546-549)
question_patterns: a factory employs 45 women; by how many does it cross the creche threshold set by the Factories Act
how many workers above thirty must an industry have before a creche becomes compulsory
find the excess over the creche trigger when an industrial unit reports W women on its rolls
a unit has exactly 30 women workers; what is the value of women_above_limit and is a creche required
calculate by what margin a workforce of 72 women exceeds the number that makes a creche mandatory
state the strength above which Section 48 of the Factories Act applies and express the excess for a plant with E women

solution_steps.action: subtract the threshold from the women employed
solution_steps.explain: the Act bites only beyond thirty women, so the excess decides the duty

worked_examples.q: Under the Factories Act Section 48, more than how many women employees trigger the creche rule: thirty or three?

concepts.title: Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise
concepts.section: Organised Efforts for Empowerment of Women
concepts.definition: When a women's collective reports its sales in crores, each member's share of the business can be found by converting the turnover to rupees and dividing it across the whole membership.
concepts.key_idea: One crore carries one crore rupees, so scale the turnover before dividing by members.
question_patterns: a women's collective of 45000 members sells goods worth 1600 crores a year; find the average sale per member in rupees
how much annual business does each member bring in when total sales of T crores are shared by M members
compute the per head sales value in rupees for a self employment society that logs S crores with N members
the yearly turnover of a papad making society is stated in crores; work out one member's share of the sales
find the average rupee sales contributed by a single worker when the annual turnover in crores and the membership are given

solution_steps.action: convert crores to rupees
solution_steps.explain: multiply the crore figure by one crore rupees to reach plain rupees

solution_steps.action: divide the rupee turnover across all members
solution_steps.explain: equal sharing gives the average business each member handles

worked_examples.q: How many rupees does one crore carry?

worked_examples.source_ref: lehe101.txt Factories Act creche provision, Section 48
worked_examples.question_pattern: An industrial unit keeps {women_employed} women on its rolls. By how many workers does it cross the creche threshold of thirty women?

solution_template.action: subtract the threshold from the rolls
solution_template.explain: 45 - 30 = 15, so the unit exceeds the trigger by 15 women

worked_examples.source_ref: lehe101.txt Lijjat Papad profile (sales turnover and membership figures)
